A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BridgeX-ICL study. Their main texts, figures, tables, equations and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original BLI and MRC experiments with LLaMA and Mistral, together with neuron analyses and ablations (Tables 1–4 and Appendices B–D).

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds a bridge-candidate experiment and CLQA/XNLI evaluations (Tables 2 and 5).

M1.justification: Both versions retain bidirectional probing, activation-frequency-based neuron identification, modified HSIC scoring across middle layers and bridge-language prompting. The final six-language bridge-candidate pool remains unchanged; evaluating additional candidates does not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Evaluation expands from BLI and MRC to four tasks. New Appendix B reports CLQA on six language pairs and XNLI on three, substantially extending task requirements while retaining the original language inventory and evaluations.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same comparator membership. Human source/target becomes Ph.D Source/Target, and Sharing matter becomes Sharing Matters. Correcting the stated baseline-category count from four to five does not add a method: all five were already listed and evaluated in v1.

E3.justification: The new candidate experiment evaluates the study's 15 languages as potential bridges across six retained BLI pairs. Existing model configurations, dictionary sizes, shot counts, BLI/MRC metrics and selected layer ranges remain unchanged. Detailed scoring and sampling protocols for CLQA/XNLI are not supplied.

E4.justification: New Section 5.1 and Table 2 test the rationale for restricting bridge candidates to Indo-European languages, including alternatives with non-Latin scripts. Existing probe-data and HSIC ablations, neuron deactivation, layer-selection and semantic analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or comparable uncertainty estimates. The additional result rows do not change the statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 2 and 5 add bridge-candidate scores and outcomes for two additional tasks. Table 5 reports CLQA deltas ranging from -0.60 to +6.20 and XNLI deltas from +0.60 to +3.70 against its zero-shot baselines. The corresponding BLI, MRC and ablation tables retain their earlier numerical values.

T1.justification: The neuron-set definitions, HSIC selection calculations and Glottolog similarity formulas retain their mathematical substance. Renaming the modified HSIC score H and making IoU cardinalities explicit are notation clarifications; no new theoretical result or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions broaden the claimed validation from two tasks to four and add the finding that non-Latin-script languages can be effective bridges. The central novelty claim about overlap-neuron-guided zero-shot bridge selection remains unchanged.

C2.justification: The limitations now explicitly acknowledge that bridge selection reflects models' training biases. Appendix E corrects v1 Appendix D's erroneous same-family interpretation of Hebrew and Tagalog, instead distinguishing clustered Portuguese–Spanish–Italian controls from dispersed Hebrew–Tagalog–Swahili controls.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability statement and replaces the anonymous BLI dictionary link with a named GitHub link. It clarifies non-overlapping neuron controls and corrects the MRC template's translation destination to the bridge language, matching the worked example already present in v1.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive research positioning are retained. Nazi (2025) versus Al Nazi (2024), and Grattafiori (2024) versus Dubey (2024), identify the same respective works by title; these are bibliographic updates rather than additions or replacements.

P1.justification: Copyediting, terminology revisions and expanded method and appendix explanations improve the prose. A candidate-selection subsection and supplementary-task appendix are inserted, with subsequent sections relabeled, while the main narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 2 and 5, improves heatmap resolution, annotates Figure 5 and enlarges and rearranges Figure 12's existing panels. Tables and appendix figures move, and Figure 11's caption is corrected from Indonesian–Tagalog to Indonesian–Hebrew.

improvement.justification: The candidate-bridge experiment, corrected semantic discussion and clearer figures address specific weaknesses in v1. Additional task results and code-access information also help. These benefits outweigh limited new inconsistencies, but the gain is constrained by under-specified CLQA/XNLI protocols and conflicting Mistral English-bridge counts: seven in the introduction and Table 3, versus six in Section 5.2.
